question: What limits xs's small-file copies between the Pi and freya, and is its best setting safe as the default?

nodes.question: Does freya's disk slow down copies from the Pi?
nodes.hypothesis: xs copies small trees into RAM on freya no faster than onto its NVMe: the receiver's disk is not the limit.
nodes.decision: K2a: RAM on freya is not clearly faster than its NVMe: the Pi sending is the limit

nodes.question: Does the Pi's own disk slow down copies to it?
nodes.hypothesis: xs copies small trees into RAM on the Pi much faster than onto its NVMe: the Pi's filesystem is the limit.
nodes.decision: K2b: into RAM on the Pi is at least 15% faster than onto its disk: the Pi's write path matters (small-flat freya→neo-shm xs-z-best 1.81× vs K1-congress-ceiling xs-z-best)

nodes.question: Can a receive-side setting on freya make up for its disk?
nodes.hypothesis: A different receiving worker count or larger writes on freya make small trees from the Pi land faster.
no receive-path setting on freya beat xs's best

nodes.question: Can a sending setting get more out of the Pi?
nodes.hypothesis: Turning compression off, leaving ssh a core, or batching reads makes the Pi send small trees faster.
no sending setting on the Pi beat xs's best

nodes.question: Can fewer workers or larger writes help the Pi's disk?
nodes.hypothesis: Fewer receiving workers or larger writes make small trees land on the Pi faster.
no receive-path setting on the Pi beat xs's best

nodes.question: Is xs's best small-file setting safe as the default for mixed trees?
nodes.hypothesis: xs's best small-file setting is no slower than its default on mixed trees, either way.

nodes.question: Which half of the best setting costs time: four workers or --no-atomic?
nodes.hypothesis: Only one half of the best small-file setting slows mixed trees on the wired pair.

nodes.question: Does the best setting also speed up no-op copies of small trees?
nodes.hypothesis: xs's best small-file setting is faster than its default on no-op copies of small trees.
xs's best setting was faster on no-op copies too
xs's best setting did not speed up no-op copies

nodes.question: Is adaptive compression the right choice on the Pi for small text trees?
nodes.hypothesis: Forcing zstd level 1, or no compression, sends small text trees from the Pi faster than adaptive -z.
adaptive -z held its own on the Pi

nodes.question: Does freya's winning receive setting hold up with fresh blocks?
nodes.hypothesis: Confirms the fastest arm of D2 with 12 fresh blocks, if it had one.

nodes.question: Does the Pi's winning send setting hold up with fresh blocks?
nodes.hypothesis: Confirms the fastest arm of D3 with 12 fresh blocks, if it had one.

nodes.question: Does the Pi's winning receive setting hold up with fresh blocks?
nodes.hypothesis: Confirms the fastest arm of D4 with 12 fresh blocks, if it had one.

nodes.question: Does the winning compression choice hold up with fresh blocks?
nodes.hypothesis: Confirms the fastest arm of D8 with 12 fresh blocks, if it had one.

nodes.question: Do the main results hold steady from run to run over the weekend?
nodes.hypothesis: xs's best setting with -z stays ahead of rsync -az from run to run.
